hint: The named bare pauses of the test trees - guard "bare pauses" in server/backend/test/clock-counts.test.js (kind 3; what counts and what does not is in its header). Per entry: file (repo-relative), count (that many bare pauses the guard counts there) and the reason from the code. The list may only SHRINK: red are a new file with a pause, a risen count, a count above the measured one (shrink along, delete at 0), an entry without a reason and one without a file.

entries.reason: Two `setTimeout(r, 0)` before the "alive" line: one ROUND of the event loop, not a duration. An unhandled rejection is processed at the end of the microtask round, i.e. before any timer; load shifts when the round comes, not the order (comment at the spot).

Five are the subject under test: a SLOW hook or switch (5-20 ms in the registered callback) at which wait:true/false show whether it is serialized - what is checked are order and a lower bound (>= 15 ms), never an upper bound. The sixth (`await sleep(20)` in the test "rejected promise with wait:false") waits for the log line of the 5 ms rejection: load-proof only because Node fires the earlier timer first and the line arises in its microtasks; replaceable by an event on the log.

`reverb()` (400 ms) at the end of four tests: an absence window in which an ASYNCHRONOUS stream error (EPIPE) should still attach to its own test instead of the next (comment at `reverb`). If it comes later under load it may land at the neighbor. Left open; replaceable by waiting for the end of the stream instead of the clock.

`LINGER_MS` (400 ms) after quiet and the `quiet()` hook, before the recorder reads the history. Does NOT run in the gate (called by hand); a too short linger shows as a deviation of the flutter probe, not as a green test. Replaceable by the stream barrier as in the golden harness.

200 ms in the scenario "join" between the mark "deltas-out" and the second message: the server reads the fake CLI's pipe asynchronously. Runs only in the recorder (the gate reads only the table `SCENARIOS`), and the `connected` after it is CHECKED - if the time does not suffice, the scenario aborts loudly instead of recording wrongly (comment at the spot).

Three synchronizations over the clock before a process count (pgrep): 400 ms after the deadline, then "no grandchild"; 700 ms after the start of the helper, then "grandchild runs"; 1,200 ms after SIGINT, then "no grandchild". Under load each of them can turn red (kill or start not through yet) - exactly what the rule forbids; replaceable by pgrep in a wait loop until the expected count.
